provenance.source_title: Towards Attuned AI: Integrating Care Ethics in Large Language Model Development and Alignment

research_problem.text: How can the ethics of care inform LLM development and value alignment when existing approaches overlook individual circumstances, relationships, and vulnerability?

central_claims.text: Integrating care ethics into LLM design and alignment offers a richer, more contextually grounded normative foundation.

evidence.text: We argue that integrating care ethics into the design and value alignment (VA) processes of LLMs offers a richer and more contextually grounded normative foundation for generative AI systems.

central_claims.text: Care ethics is necessary, not merely relevant, to the future responsible development of LLMs.

evidence.text: we aim to show why EoC is not only a relevant but necessary ethical foundation for the future of responsible LLMs' development.

central_claims.text: Mainstream alignment frameworks frequently overlook the situated, affective, and power-sensitive aspects of moral life emphasized by care ethics.

evidence.text: these frameworks frequently overlook the situated, affective, and power-sensitive dimensions of moral life that EoC brings to the foreground.

central_claims.text: Care ethics' attention to particular needs and vulnerabilities makes it particularly well suited to LLM interactions in which providing care is fundamental, such as mental health support.

evidence.text: Unlike frameworks grounded in impartiality and universality, EoC focuses on particular needs and vulnerabilities, making it particularly well-suited for LLMs deployed in domains and contexts where providing care is a fundamental aspect of the interaction, such as mental health support.

central_claims.text: Care ethics can counter the moral distancing associated with automation and algorithmic decision-making.

evidence.text: By resisting abstraction and centering relationality, EoC challenges the moral distancing introduced by automation and algorithmic decision-making

central_claims.text: Care ethics' compatibility with Ubuntu makes it a powerful decolonial alternative to dominant AI ethics frameworks.

evidence.text: Its compatibility with non-Western ethical traditions such as Ubuntu, "I am because we are", also makes it a powerful decolonial alternative to dominant AI ethics frameworks

citations.reference_entry: Lameck Mbangula Amugongo, Nicola J. Bidwell, and Caitlin C. Corrigan. Invigorating Ubuntu Ethics in AI for healthcare: Enabling equitable care. In 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, pages 583-592, Chicago IL USA, June 2023. ACM.

central_claims.text: LLMs' application of overly generalized patterns can fail to meet individual needs and social contexts, making the models ethically inadequate in emotionally sensitive domains.

evidence.text: these models often fail to respond appropriately to individual needs and social contexts because they apply overly generalized patterns of reasoning. This failure makes them ethically inadequate in emotionally sensitive domains.

central_claims.text: A static, well-defined training distribution cannot adequately represent the dynamic, complex real world in which LLMs operate; situations treated as edge cases therefore expose a gap between controlled generalization and real-world performance.

evidence.text: the core issue lies in the very concept of a well-defined 'training data set distribution' being representative of the dynamic and complex real world.

Consequently, the performance of FFNNs in these seemingly 'edge' scenarios becomes a crucial consideration, highlighting a significant gap between theoretical capabilities within controlled distributions and the unpredictable nature of real-world applications.

central_claims.text: LLMs inherit generalization vulnerabilities from feed-forward neural networks and can produce biased, context-insensitive, or inappropriate outputs.

evidence.text: As such, they are vulnerable to the same generalization problems. We see this in practice through empirical evidence that LLMs frequently exhibit representational biases and produce context-insensitive or inappropriate outputs, a problem extensively documented in recent work

citations.reference_entry: Roberto Navigli, Simone Conia, and Bjorn Ross. Biases in Large Language Models: Origins, Inventory, and Discussion. J. Data and Information Quality, 15(2):10:1-10:21, June 2023.

central_claims.text: Models can replicate harmful biases in care-relevant settings: the paper points to discriminatory therapy-chatbot responses, gender-stereotyped storytelling, and benefit-assessment systems reproducing existing human bias.

evidence.text: Illustrative of the inherent limitations of relying on abstract generalizations in Large Language Models (LLMs) is their propensity to replicate harmful societal biases across critical domains.
In the realm of mental health, research has shown therapy chatbots exhibiting discriminatory responses based on users' conditions, perpetuating harmful stigmas

citations.reference_entry: Maggie Harrison Dupre. Stanford Research Finds That "Therapist" Chatbots Are Encouraging Users' Schizophrenic Delusions and Suicidal Thoughts. futurism.com, June 2025.

evidence.text: LLMs have been found to generate narratives that reinforce traditional stereotypes in storytelling

citations.reference_entry: UCL. Large Language Models generate biased content, warn researchers. ucl.ac.uk, April 2024.

evidence.text: attempts to implement AI for fairer benefit assessments have resulted in the reproduction of existing human biases

citations.reference_entry: Yufei Guo, Muzhe Guo, Juntao Su, Zhou Yang, Mengqiu Zhu, Hongfei Li, Mengyang Qiu, and Shuo Shuo Liu. Bias in Large Language Models: Origin, Evaluation, and Mitigation, November 2024.

central_claims.text: Bias arises not only from training data but also from subjective values in human and AI alignment feedback.

evidence.text: This bias is not solely a product of flawed training data but also arises from the subjective values embedded in human and even AI feedback during alignment processes.

central_claims.text: The ethically important defect is not whether model rules are simple or intricate, but whether their internal logic tracks the particularities that matter in real-world contexts.

evidence.text: The issue is not that these models operate on "simple" or "complicated" rules, but rather that their internal logic frequently fails to track the particularities that matter in real-world contexts, no matter how intricate it is.

central_claims.text: LLM training and design should prioritize individual and contextual particularities rather than statistical generalization; this shift could mitigate harms from misapplied generalizations.

evidence.text: Re-thinking the training and design of LLMs through the lens of EoC would entail prioritizing individual and contextual particularities rather than optimizing for statistical generalization. This shift could help mitigate the harmful consequences of misapplied generalizations and align AI systems more closely with the nuanced moral demands of human interaction.

central_claims.text: RLHF and RLAIF embed particular, non-neutral normative commitments: aggregated human preferences and predefined fairness or constitutional principles reflect utilitarian and justice-based approaches.

evidence.text: These approaches optimize behaviour either by aggregating human preferences (in RLHF), or by aligning model outputs with predefined fairness metrics or constitutional principles (in RLAIF), thus reflecting a commitment to maximizing overall utility or ensuring procedural fairness

citations.reference_entry: Andrew Sola. Utilitarianism and Consequentialist Ethics: Framing the Greater Good. In Ethics and Pandemics: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on COVID-19 and Future Pandemics, pages 61-83. Springer Nature Switzerland, 2023.

evidence.text: These moral commitments, however, are not value-neutral.

central_claims.text: In care contexts, utilitarian approaches may justify sacrificing an individual's well-being for aggregate benefit.

evidence.text: Utilitarian approaches may justify sacrificing individual well-being for the sake of aggregated good, which is ethically troubling in contexts such as mental health or healthcare, where individual vulnerability and situational complexity demand more than mere utility maximization

citations.reference_entry: Andrew Sola. Utilitarianism and Consequentialist Ethics: Framing the Greater Good. In Ethics and Pandemics: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on COVID-19 and Future Pandemics, pages 61-83. Springer Nature Switzerland, 2023.

central_claims.text: Justice-based approaches may overemphasize truthfulness or impartiality at the expense of emotional, relational, and contextual needs.

evidence.text: justice-based approaches may overemphasize principles such as truthfulness or impartiality, and fail to account for the emotional, relational, and context-sensitive needs of individuals in morally complex or care-relevant situations

citations.reference_entry: Carol Gilligan. In a Different Voice: Psychological Theory and Women's Development. Harvard University Press, 1993.

central_claims.text: Reward maximization and rule-following do not reflect the relational, context-sensitive character of human moral decision-making, making current alignment frameworks inadequate in care settings.

evidence.text: But this moral calculus does not reflect how humans actually make ethical decisions.
In such settings, the current VA frameworks, grounded in rule-following and aggregation, prove inadequate.

central_claims.text: Anthropic's Constitutional AI presents a deontological commitment in its constitution, but its reward-maximizing implementation operates on utilitarian principles.

evidence.text: Thus, Anthropic's framework presents a deontological front, but its mechanics operate on utilitarian principles.
At this stage, an AI preference model trained to align with the constitution provides reward signals, and the system is optimized to maximize these signals

citations.reference_entry: Yuntao Bai et al. Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback, December 2022.

central_claims.text: The technical implementation of Anthropic's purportedly deontological alignment approach could only be utilitarian.

evidence.text: although in principle, Anthropic adopted a deontological approach to value alignment, the technical implementation could only be utilitarian.

central_claims.text: It is necessary to develop an ethics-of-care-inspired alignment method tailored to care-relevant domains and contexts.

evidence.text: Therefore, we argue that it is necessary to develop a value alignment method tailored to care-relevant domains and contexts inspired by the ethics of care.

central_claims.text: Care-informed feedback for a mental-health chatbot would attend to the user's emotional state, relational cues, and expressed needs rather than merely reward generally preferred traits; for a user expressing suicidal thoughts, it might prioritize empathy, safety, and relational responsibility over truthfulness.

evidence.text: However, a care ethics-informed chatbot would go further by weighing feedback according to the user's current unique emotional state, relational cues, and expressed needs. A distressed user expressing suicidal thoughts might receive an AI response that prioritizes empathy, the user's safety, and relational responsibility over truthfulness.

central_claims.text: Care-based alignment would train models to respond to users' emotional, social, and contextual needs, rather than merely to reward signals.

evidence.text: A care-based VA approach would train systems not merely to be reward-sensitive, but to be morally attentive, i.e. responsive to the emotional, social, and contextual needs of users.

central_claims.text: Care ethics would guide processes such as RLAIF to consider relational context and potential harms to vulnerable individuals and communities.

evidence.text: Rather than optimizing for abstract utility or procedural fairness, care ethics would guide alignment processes like RLAIF to consider the specific relational context and potential harms to vulnerable individuals and communities.

central_claims.text: Care ethics would encourage human labelers to consider the broader relational effects of AI responses, particularly for marginalized or care-dependent populations.

evidence.text: It would also inform the work of human labelers, encouraging them to reflect not only on individual preferences, but on the broader relational impacts of AI responses, especially for marginalized or care-dependent populations.

central_claims.text: Care ethics could enrich constitutional approaches by promoting the well-being of caregivers and care-receivers within interdependent social networks.

evidence.text: Constitutionally, care ethics could provide a richer moral foundation by promoting the well-being of both caregivers and care-receivers within interdependent social networks.

central_claims.text: Embedding a care orientation would make LLM chatbots more likely to resist sycophancy, minimize hallucinations, and engage users with greater responsibility and trust.

evidence.text: By embedding this moral orientation, LLM's chatbots would be more likely to resist sycophantic behaviour, minimize hallucinations, and engage users with a deeper sense of responsibility and trust.

central_claims.text: Care ethics better reflects how people want to be treated in morally significant AI interactions.

evidence.text: By offering a context-sensitive and relationally grounded framework, care ethics better reflects how people actually want to be treated in morally significant interactions with AI.

methodology.summary: Conceptual ethics and value-alignment argument organized around two lines of reasoning: harms associated with LLM generalization and the normative limitations of existing alignment methods. The paper uses cited literature, examples from care-relevant applications, and Constitutional AI as an illustrative case; it does not present an implemented alignment method or original empirical evaluation.
data_sources: Cited work on care ethics, neural-network generalization, LLM bias, and value alignment
Illustrative examples involving mental health, gender, social services, and Constitutional AI
methodology.sample_or_scope: LLM development and alignment, especially mental health, education, eldercare, and social services
analysis_methods: Normative comparison of care ethics with utilitarian and justice-based approaches
Analysis of RLHF, RLAIF, and Constitutional AI

assumptions.text: The particularities of a user's vulnerability and relationships are morally salient features that LLM alignment should recognize.
Care-sensitive behavior can, at least in part, be fostered through changes to training, feedback interpretation, or reinforcement, even though the authors have not specified a full implementation.

limitations.text: Care ethics' contextual and relational character resists formalization and scalability, while its lack of procedural structure may hinder transparency and consistency in automated systems.
The paper does not elaborate a full technical methodology for modifying alignment methods to incorporate care principles.
Recognizing and responding to complex emotional and social cues remains technically underdeveloped; current models lack genuine understanding of vulnerability, dependency, and relational dynamics.
The predicted reduction in sycophancy and hallucinations is asserted in the conclusion without an implementation or evaluation demonstrating those effects.

proposed_solutions.text: Adapt LLM design and alignment strategies to accommodate care ethics rather than excluding it because it is difficult to formalize.
Modify RLHF or RLAIF so feedback and reinforcement attend to an interaction's individual and contextual moral significance rather than generic reward maximization.
Train models in care-relevant interactions to identify signs of vulnerability, dependency, and self-harm and adjust responses accordingly.
Incorporate care considerations into constitutional frameworks and human-labeling practices, including attention to caregivers, care-receivers, and the relational effects of responses.

open_questions.text: What full technical methodology could implement care-based value alignment in RLHF, RLAIF, or related systems?
How can care ethics' contextual, relational reasoning be operationalized while maintaining transparency, consistency, and scalability?
How can LLMs reliably recognize emotional and social cues and respond to vulnerability without genuine understanding of relational dynamics?
